subject: Pipeline commands (awk/tr/wc/sort/grep) are a second Linux surface in Windows boxes
description: Found 2026-09-12 while fixing the Terminal.js builtin leak (SHELL-004). Terminal.js exposes a SECOND command surface beyond the builtin dispatcher: _splitPipeSegments / the pipeline handler implements awk, tr, wc, sort and friends around _app/arena/engine/Terminal.js:436-480. These are reachable only inside a pipe (e.g. 'echo x | wc -l'), so they are NOT covered by SHELL-004, which derives its required list from the builtin switch between the '// Built-in commands' marker and its 'default:'. An early version of SHELL-004 matched every 'case' in the whole file, swept these in, and produced 68 findings demanding boxes override commands they never receive directly — that was noise and was scoped out deliberately, NOT because the underlying concern is invalid. THE CONCERN IS REAL: a student in a cmd.exe or PowerShell sim who types a pipeline gets GNU awk/wc behaviour, which is the same defect class as 'id' answering with a POSIX uid string. It is lower severity because it requires the student to construct a pipe, and pipes are themselves a Unix idiom a Windows-sim student is less likely to reach for. Decide: either give the pipeline handler the same per-style treatment (cmd.exe has no awk/wc/sort; PowerShell has Select-String/Measure-Object/Sort-Object), or document that pipelines are intentionally Unix-flavoured everywhere. Do NOT just extend SHELL-004's derived range to the whole file — that reintroduces the 68 false findings.
